arxiv-2007-02674.title: Sensor Data and the City: Urban Visualisation and Aggregation of Well-Being Data DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: UbiComp ’20; September 12–16, 2020; Cancun, Mexico Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Human-centered computing Geographic visualization
arxiv-2007-02674.creator: Thomas Johnson, Eiman Kanjo, Kieran Woodward
arxiv-2007-02674.description: Abstract . The growth of mobile sensor technologies have made it possible for city councils to understand peoples’ behaviour in urban spaces which could help to reduce stress around the city. We present a quantitative approach to convey a collective sense of urban places.

arxiv-2007-04009.title: A Tukey type trend test for repeated carcinogenicity bioassays, motivated by multiple glyphosate studies
arxiv-2007-04009.creator: Ludwig A. Hothorn, Frank Schaarschmidt
arxiv-2007-04009.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Ludwig A. Hothorn, Frank Schaarschmidt. In the last two decades, significant methodological progress to the simultaneous inference of simple and complex randomized designs, particularly proportions as endpoints, occurred. This includes: i) the new Tukey trend test approach [ 7 ] , ii) multiple contrast tests for binomial proportions [ 14 ] , iii) multiple contrast tests for poly-k estimates [ 15 ] , and Add-1 approximation for one-sided inference [ 13 ] .

arxiv-2109-10054.creator: Mingyao Cui, , Linglong Dai
arxiv-2109-10054.description: Abstract The natural integration of extremely large antenna arrays (ELAAs) and terahertz (THz) communications can potentially establish Tbps data links for 6G networks. However, due to the extremely large array aperture and wide bandwidth, a new phenomenon termed as “near-field beam split” emerges.

arxiv-2112-11686.title: Parametrized Complexity of Quantum Inspired Algorithms
arxiv-2112-11686.creator: Ebrahim Ardeshir-Larijani*
arxiv-2112-11686.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ebrahim Ardeshir-Larijani*. 1 Introduction Motivated by recent progress in quantum technologies and in particular quantum software, research and industrial communities have been trying to discover new applications of quantum algorithms such as quantum optimization and machine learning. Regardless of which hardware platform these novel algorithms operate on, whether it is adiabatic or gate based , from theoretical point of view, they are performing drastically better than their classical counterparts.

arxiv-2302-10525.title: Molecular chaos in dense active systems
arxiv-2302-10525.creator: Lu Chen, Kyle J. Welch, Premkumar Leishangthem, Dipanjan Ghosh, Bokai Zhang, Ting-Pi Sun, Josh Klukas, Zhanchun Tu, Xiang Cheng, Xinliang Xu
arxiv-2302-10525.description: Abstract The hypothesis of molecular chaos plays the central role in kinetic theory, which provides a closure leading to the Boltzmann equation for quantitative description of classic fluids. Yet how to properly extend it to active systems is still an open question in nonequilibrium physics.

arxiv-2304-00175.title: Well-posedness and qualitative properties of quasilinear degenerate evolution systems
arxiv-2304-00175.creator: K. Mitra, S. Sonner
arxiv-2304-00175.description: Abstract We analyze nonlinear degenerate coupled PDE-PDE and PDE-ODE systems that arise, for example, in the modelling of biofilm growth. One of the equations, describing the evolution of a biomass density, exhibits degenerate and singular diffusion. The other equations are either of advection-reaction-diffusion type or ordinary differential equations.

arxiv-2407-13764.title: Shape of Motion: 4D Reconstruction from a Single Video
arxiv-2407-13764.creator: Qianqian Wang*, Vickie Ye, Hang Gao, Jake Austin, Zhengqi Li, Angjoo Kanazawa, [6pt] 1 UC Berkeley 2 Google Research
arxiv-2407-13764.description: Abstract Monocular dynamic reconstruction is a challenging and long-standing vision problem due to the highly ill-posed nature of the task. Existing approaches are limited in that they either depend on templates, are effective only in quasi-static scenes, or fail to model 3D motion explicitly.

arxiv-2502-11043.title: Analysis of the autocorrelation function for time series with higher-order temporal correlations: An exponential case
arxiv-2502-11043.creator: Min-ho Yu, Hang-Hyun Jo
arxiv-2502-11043.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Min-ho Yu, Hang-Hyun Jo. Temporal correlations in the time series observed in various systems have been characterized by the autocorrelation function. Such correlations can be explained by heavy-tailed interevent time distributions as well as by correlations between interevent times. The latter is called higher-order temporal correlations, and they have been captured by the notion of bursts; a burst indicates a set of consecutive events that rapidly occur within a short time period and are separated from other bursts by long time intervals.

arxiv-2505-05935.title: List-Recovery of Random Linear Codes over Small Fields
arxiv-2505-05935.creator: Dean Doron, Jonathan Mosheiff, Nicolas Resch, João Ribeiro
arxiv-2505-05935.description: Abstract We study list-recoverability of random linear codes over small fields, both from errors and from erasures. We consider codes of rate ε \varepsilon -close to capacity, and aim to bound the dependence of the output list size L L on ε \varepsilon , the input list size ℓ \ell , and the alphabet size q q .

arxiv-2509-05931.title: Quantization of bounded symplectic domains associated with compact Lie groups
arxiv-2509-05931.description: Abstract We present a systematic quantization scheme for bounded symplectic domains of the form D × G ⊂ T ∗ ​ G D\times G\subset T^{\ast}G , where D ⊂ 𝔤 ∗ D\subset\mathfrak{g}^{\ast} is a bounded region defined by algebraic inequalities and G G is a compact Lie group with Lie algebra 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} .

arxiv-2601-04650.title: Explainable machine learning classification of Chandra X-ray sources: SHAP analysis of multi-wavelength features Journal: ApJ Facilities: CXO astropy ( 5 ; 3 ; 4 ) , LightGBM ( 22 ; 43 ) , scikit-learn ( 8 ) , scipy ( 49 ) , Matplotlib ( 20 )
arxiv-2601-04650.creator: Shivam Kumaran, Samir Mandal, Sudip Bhattacharyya
arxiv-2601-04650.description: Abstract Extensive astronomical surveys, like those conducted with the Chandra X-ray Observatory, detect hundreds of thousands of unidentified cosmic sources. Machine learning (ML) methods offer an efficient, probabilistic approach to classify them, which can be useful for making discoveries and conducting deeper studies.

plos-pone-0001580.creator: Nicolas Mathevon, Thierry Aubin, Jacques Vielliard et al.
plos-pone-0001580.description: PLOS ONE research article. pmc-10577267.title: Genome sequencing of SARS-CoV-2 omicron variants in Delhi reveals alterations in immunogenic regions in spike glycoprotein
pmc-10577267.creator: Sristy Shikha, Mukesh Kumar Jogi, Ruchika Jha, Rana Amit Kumar, Tathagat Sah, Pushpendra Singh, Ritu Sagar, Anuj Kumar, Robin Marwal, Kalaiarasan Ponnusamy, Subhash Mohan Agarwal, R. Suresh Kumar, Nazneen Arif, Mausumi Bharadwaj, Shalini Singh, Pramod Kumar
pmc-10577267.description: The SARS-CoV-2 omicron variants keep accumulating a large number of mutations in the spike (S) protein, which contributes to greater transmissibility and a rapid rise to dominance within populations. The identification of mutations and their affinity to the cellular angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 (ACE-2) receptor and immune evasion in the Delhi NCR region was under-acknowledged.

pmc-10585338.title: Significant vomiting and weight loss in a pediatric epilepsy patient secondary to vagus nerve stimulation: A case report and review of the literature
pmc-10585338.creator: Hannah E Snyder, Nikhil Pai, Brandon Meaney, Cynthia Sloan Birbeck, Robyn Whitney, Natasha Johnson, Laura Rosato, Kevin Jones
pmc-10585338.description: Highlights•Vagus nerve stimulation is a treatment option for drug-resistant epilepsy.•While vomiting and weight loss have been described with VNS treatment, these are typically mild.•The relationship between the vagus nerve and gastrointestinal motility is well-described.•Our patient experienced profound vomiting and weight loss due to VNS.

pmc-10709196.title: Unveiling the mechanisms of nephrotoxicity caused by nephrotoxic compounds using toxicological network analysis
pmc-10709196.creator: Kexing Xi, Mengqing Zhang, Mingrui Li, Qiang Tang, Qi Zhao, Wei Chen
pmc-10709196.description: Billions of people worldwide have experienced irreversible kidney injuries, which is mainly attributed to the complexity of drug-induced nephrotoxicity. Consequently, there is an urgent need for uncovering the mechanisms of nephrotoxicity caused by compounds. In the present study, a network-based methodology was applied to explore the mechanisms of nephrotoxicity induced by specific compounds.

pmc-11461077.title: Aloperine Ameliorates Acetaminophen-Induced Acute Liver Injury through HMGB1/TLR4/NF-κB and NLRP3/Inflammasome Pathway
pmc-11461077.creator: Hui Chen, Shu Wang, Qiuyue Chen, Wen Yu, Hao Nie, Lian Liu, Bing Zheng, Quan Gong
pmc-11461077.description: Purpose Aloperine (ALO), an alkaloid isolated from Sophora alopecuroides L., possesses multiple pharmacological activities and holds a promise potential for the treatment of various clinical conditions, including skin hypersensitivity, cancer, and inflammatory disorders. The purpose of this study was to investigate the role of ALO in acetaminophen (N-acetyl-para-aminophenol (APAP))-induced acute liver injury and its underlying mechanisms.

pmc-11676039.title: Imported Fire Ants Discard Cricket Eggs
pmc-11676039.creator: Jian Chen, Xinzhi Ni, Michael J Grodowitz, Allen Carson Cohen
pmc-11676039.description: Simple SummaryDuring routine feeding of crickets to laboratory imported fire ant colonies, it was observed that while most of the cricket tissues are used by the fire ants, only the hard outside shell or cuticle and the eggs are not utilized. Interestingly, the eggs are removed from the nest and deposited on refuse piles created by the fire ants.

pmc-12361400.title: Nucleic acid amplification tests in digital microfluidics: the promise of next-generation point-of-care diagnostics
pmc-12361400.creator: Duc Anh Thai, Yuguang Liu
pmc-12361400.description: Nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT) have long been used in laboratory facilities and recently revolutionized the field of molecular diagnostics in point-of-care testing. Digital microfluidics (DMF) has emerged as a promising tool to complete the entire NAAT workflow in a miniaturized format with minimum human intervention.

pmc-12650142.title: Compensatory Failure of Autonomic Regulation in Phantom Limb Pain and Its Correlation with Maladaptive Plasticity: A Cross-Sectional HRV Study in Amputees
pmc-12650142.creator: Nadine Aranis, Eneidy Piña Mojica, Jean Alex Matos Ribeiro, David Sparrow, David Crandell, Anna Lepesteur Gianlorenco, Felipe Fregni, Maria Venihaki
pmc-12650142.description: Background/Objectives: Chronic pain is associated with autonomic nervous system (ANS) dysfunction, which can be indexed by heart rate variability (HRV). This cross-sectional study examined associations between ANS dysregulation and phantom limb pain (PLP) intensity in amputees and explored related clinical and psychosocial variables. Methods: Fifty-three adults with chronic PLP (mean age 57.7 ± 15.4; 60% male) were enrolled.

pmc-12742205.title: Global burden of disease analysis and projections of ischemic stroke linked to inadequate polyunsaturated fatty acid intake in older women (1990–2021)
pmc-12742205.creator: Ying Luo, Guoliang Zhu, Quandan Tan, Yapeng Lin, Jie Yang
pmc-12742205.description: BackgroundIschemic stroke (IS), a major global cause of death and disability, is significantly influenced by diet. While polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) exhibits neuroprotective effects, the specific stroke burden attributable to inadequate PUFA intake among women ≥ 50 years remains unquantified.

pmc-12858935.title: Reconstruction of 2,965 Microbial Genomes from Mangrove Sediments across Guangxi, China
pmc-12858935.creator: Ying Liu, Songze Chen, Huiquan Li, Nazia Mahtab, Yue Sun, Yunru Li, Jingjing Song, Dan Sun, Mingzhong Liang, Jianqing Chen, Jing Sun, Bin Gong, Jiaojiao Jing, Rongping Bu
pmc-12858935.description: Mangrove sediments, being organic-rich and anoxic, host diverse and functionally important microorganisms that play crucial roles in global biogeochemical cycling. In order to characterize this diversity at the genome-resolved level, we collected 38 sediment samples encompassing both surface (0–5 cm) and core (up to 90 cm) depths from six representative mangrove sites across Guangxi Province, China.

pmc-13077836.title: The association between resilience and athletic performance: findings from a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies
pmc-13077836.creator: Zhengyang Mei, Chenyi Cai, Chifong Lam, Tingfeng Wang, Haichang Jiang, Shi Luo
pmc-13077836.description: ObjectiveThis systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively synthesize existing evidence regarding the overall correlation between resilience and athletic performance and explore potential moderating variables.MethodsObservational studies of the association between resilience and athletic performance were identified using electronic databases and manual searches.

pmc-13335545.title: Cold Orthogonal Translation: A Psychrophilic Pyrrolysyl‐tRNA Synthetase Boosts Genetic Code Expansion in E. coli
pmc-13335545.creator: Nikolaj G Koch, Peter Goettig, Michael A Nash, Juri Rappsilber, Nediljko Budisa
pmc-13335545.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Orthogonal translation systems (OTSs) enable site‐specific incorporation of non‐canonical amino acids (ncAAs) and are central to genetic code expansion. Current engineering strategies typically rely on hyperstable aminoacyl tRNA synthetase (aaRS) scaffolds to tolerate destabilizing mutations required for substrate diversification. Here, we introduce an alternative design principle: exploiting the intrinsic conformational flexibility of a psychrophilic pyrrolysyl‐tRNA synthetase (PylRS) enzyme to enhance mutational tolerance and in vivo performance.

pmc-13635098.title: Perceived humanness and empathy are dissociated in relationship advice generated by a large language model
pmc-13635098.creator: Bennett Kleinberg, Jari Zegers, Jonas Festor, Stefana Vida, Julian Präsent, Riccardo Loconte, Sanne Peereboom
pmc-13635098.description: Differentiating generated and human-written content is increasingly difficult. We examine how incentives to convey humanness and task characteristics shape perceptions of textual content across five studies. In Studies 1–2, humans and GPT-4 write relationship advice or relationship descriptions with or without instructions to appear human. New participants judge each text’s source.
